varieties.description: Tall, strongly fragrant cut flower stock with 32" stems and very early, programmable timing (7–11 weeks in fall, 8–13 weeks in spring). Uniform stem length across the mix. Approximately 50% double flowering, which is normal for stock. Best suited for cool greenhouse, tunnel, or open field.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Can also be sown January–February as an insurance sowing using the same seed. Grows best in cool, bright conditions — cold frame or unheated greenhouse, not a warm house.

varieties.description: Classic 30" cut flower snapdragon, fragrant, with strong upright spikes suited for field or greenhouse production. The Rocket series is a standard professional cut flower choice. Available in individual colours (Bronze, Golden Yellow, Orchid, Pink, Red, White) and mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also sow January–February for a second wave. Needs cool, bright conditions to develop strong stems.

varieties.description: Tall double azalea-flowered snapdragon, 30", described as a superb cut flower. F1 hybrid for uniform timing and stem quality. AAS award winner. Available in individual colours (Bronze, Ivory, Pink, Red, Yellow) and mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also suitable for a January–February insurance sowing.

varieties.description: Group IV tall snapdragon (32–40") with solid spikes on sturdy stems. Named replacement for the discontinued Costa Summer series. Well suited to greenhouse, tunnel, or open ground production.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in pots or trays under cool cover (45–55°F). Also suitable for January–February insurance sowing.

varieties.description: Giant Imperial type larkspur at 32", a reliable direct-sown cut flower. The Imperial Choice Mix is an exact match for traditional cut flower larkspur plantings. Direct sow only — taproot resents transplanting. Suited to the back of the border.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a raised, well-drained bed. Cold stratification happens naturally over winter. Most fall sowing failures are caused by poor drainage, not cold. Do not transplant.

varieties.description: Extra-select double bicolour cornflower mix suited to field-grown cut flower, borders, and mass landscape plantings. Direct sown. The Frosty Mix includes frosted bicolour tones not found in standard bachelor's button mixes.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a raised, well-drained bed. Hardy annual that benefits from cold conditioning over winter.

varieties.description: Traditional double-flowered Love-in-a-Mist, direct sown to field. Both the intricate blue-green flowers and the striped, inflated seed pods are useful in arrangements. Available in single colours (Indigo, Light Blue, White) and mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November. Taproot — does not transplant well. Scatter seed in a prepared bed.

varieties.description: 24" long-stemmed calendula with double and semi-double flowers in orange, apricot, cream, and lemon tones. A classic direct-sown cut flower. Available in single colours (Apricot, Cream, Lemon, Orange w/ Brown Eye) and mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a well-drained bed. Can also be sown in early spring. Cold-hardy and tolerant of light frost.

varieties.description: 6-foot fragrant climbing sweet pea bred specifically for cut flower production under short days — the best fit for a November sowing aimed at late April to May flowering. Available in single colours (Burgundy, Deep Rose, Mid Blue, White) and mix. Note: a Bed 3 fence row will require multiple packs as each pack is only 100 seeds.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in deep root-trainers under cool cover (45–55°F). Pre-chill seed 4 weeks at 32–35°F, then soak overnight before sowing 1" deep. Needs a trellis or fence. Quantity note: 100 seeds per Trade Pkt — plan on multiple packs for a full fence row.

varieties.description: Sweet pea mix; approximately 300 seeds per ounce. A practical choice for large-scale plantings where a named Spencer variety is not required.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow in deep root-trainers under cool cover. Pre-soak overnight. Needs a trellis or fence. Climbs to 6 feet.

varieties.description: F1 hybrid Iceland poppy, 15", with uniform timing, sturdy stems, and large flowers. Primed seed for reliable germination. Available in single colours (Orange, Pink, Scarlet, White, Yellow) and mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Sow November in individual pots — Iceland poppies strongly resent root disturbance. Keep cool and bright (cold frame or unheated greenhouse). Do not transplant bareroot.

varieties.description: 2-foot double Shirley-type poppy mix in cherry, cream, orange, lilac, and mauve bicolour tones. A fresh local cut flower classic, field sown. The American Legion (red Flanders type) is a separate variety — Angel's Choir is the Shirley mix.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow outdoors in November into a well-drained bed. Scatter seed on the surface; poppies need light to germinate. Do not bury seed deeply.

varieties.description: Low-growing front-of-border filler with fragrant small flowers.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow. Suited to front-of-border or low edging. Can be scattered in gaps between taller plants.

varieties.description: Classic ornamental and culinary poppy with large, showy flowers and ornamental seedpods useful in dried arrangements.
varieties.sowingNotes: Direct sow late fall for natural cold stratification. 1,266,000 seeds per pound. Scatter on the soil surface; needs light to germinate.

sellers.name: Songbird Seed Co.
sellers.description: Boutique seed venture of Colleen Raney (also Diadem Flower Co.), specialising in hard-to-find British sweet pea seeds grown on a small farm in Washington's Skagit Valley.
sellers.orderingNotes: Farm-grown seed packets; Hues buys from Songbird. Specialty sweet pea drops sell out quickly.

sellers.name: Sunflower Steve Seed Co.
sellers.description: Steve Kaufer, Wisconsin cut-flower grower and sunflower breeder (breeding since ~2008); sells his own bred sunflower varieties.
sellers.orderingNotes: Sells direct from its own site.

sellers.name: Floret
sellers.description: Erin Benzakein's family flower farm and seed company; breeds its own cut-flower varieties (Floret Originals).
sellers.orderingNotes: Sells seed only occasionally — periodic, limited seed sales rather than an always-open shop; availability is episodic.

sellers.name: Dawn Creek Farm
sellers.description: Kori Hargreaves' farm breeding program — zinnias since 2016, plus cynoglossum and other cut flowers. Her varieties also reach market through Floret.
sellers.orderingNotes: Episodic: an annual fundraiser window (seeds as thank-you gifts, typically limit 1 packet/person, US shipping only, ships ~March). Breeder terms: no reselling or renaming her varieties; listings credit Dawn Creek as breeder.

sellers.name: Hudson Valley Seed Co.
sellers.description: Small independent seed house in Accord, New York; grows on its own farm and works with regional small growers; known for artist-designed 'Art Pack' packets, much of the line certified organic.
sellers.orderingNotes: Standing shop (always open). Only its flower varieties are listed in this directory.

sellers.name: Wild West Seed
sellers.description: Independent Oregon seed producer in the Willamette Valley: grows flower and vegetable seed with local partner growers; wildflower mixes and contract seed production.
sellers.orderingNotes: Wholesale/bulk-oriented rather than a retail packet shop.

sellers.name: Basket of Flowers Farm
sellers.description: Family farm that saved open-pollinated zinnias from its U-Pick field in 2021 and bred the 'Dearest' series in isolated grow-outs on the farm.
sellers.orderingNotes: Episodic: seed sales close for the season and reopen in December; newsletter passcode gives early access.

sellers.name: Flower People
sellers.description: Family-run flower farm and seed company whose seed collection is built around its own cut-flower growing — 35+ sweet peas plus celosia, strawflower, snapdragon, cosmos, zinnia and larkspur.
sellers.orderingNotes: Standing Shopify shop; many varieties sold out between drops.

sellers.name: Lunaseed Farm
sellers.description: Woman-owned flower seed farm; all seed field-grown, open-pollinated, harvested and cleaned by hand. Spencer and Grandiflora sweet peas plus cottage flowers.

sellers.name: Enchanting Sweet Peas
sellers.description: One-person operation (Glenys Johnson) selling Spencer sweet peas — 40+ varieties — directly from the Sebastopol seed grower; 29 years growing and selling sweet peas.
sellers.orderingNotes: Seasonal: seed sales start in September.

sellers.name: Uprising Seeds
sellers.description: Small family-run certified organic seed farm; produces over 70% of the seed it sells at its home farm, the remainder from Pacific Northwest family farms. Specialty cut flowers, all open-pollinated.

sellers.name: Siskiyou Seeds
sellers.description: Produces open-pollinated and heirloom seed on its home farm in southwest Oregon, plus a network of certified-organic small farms in the West. Broad flower list.

sellers.name: Wild Garden Seed
sellers.description: Organic seed farm established 1994 (Frank & Karen Morton); all seed organically grown by Shoulder to Shoulder Farm, many varieties from its on-farm breeding program.

sellers.name: Adaptive Seeds
sellers.description: Certified-organic farm-based seed company (est. 2009) growing over 75% of the seed it sells on its own farm; ~120 flower listings including farm-bred and farm-selected varieties.

sellers.name: Grand Prismatic Seed
sellers.description: Small seed farm in northern Utah (co-owners James Young & Guy Banner) growing with organic methods; curated cut flowers plus dye plants and Great Basin natives.

sellers.name: Coseytown Flowers
sellers.description: Independent dahlia hybridizer (LeeAnn Huber); all dahlia seed is harvested from Coseytown's own dahlia fields.
sellers.orderingNotes: Episodic: tuber and seed sales mainly January–April with restocks.

sellers.name: Garden Bee Flower Farm
sellers.description: Paula Fisher (DBA Paula's Dahlias) saves seed from her own dahlia field, evaluates seedlings, and hand-processes every packet.

sellers.name: Turtle Tree Seed
sellers.description: Small non-profit seed company at Camphill Village; every seed grown with Demeter-certified biodynamic and organic practices. 350+ open-pollinated varieties including dahlia seed.

sellers.name: Nature and Nurture Seeds
sellers.description: Farm-based seed company near Ann Arbor; grows over 30% of its catalog on its 80-acre certified-organic farm, 60%+ in the Midwest.

sellers.name: North Circle Seeds
sellers.description: Certified-organic Midwestern grower circle producing regionally adapted, open-pollinated seed.

sellers.name: High Desert Seed + Gardens
sellers.description: High-altitude seed farm founded by Laura Parker; reported to grow ~90% of the seed it sells. Dedicated cut-flower section.

sellers.name: Larner Seeds
sellers.description: California native wildflower seed usable as cut flowers, from a one-acre demonstration garden in Bolinas growing 100+ coastal native plants for over 40 years.

sellers.name: Mountainlily Farm
sellers.description: Single horticulturist and licensed Ozark nursery; heirloom flower seed — celosia mixes, mixed sunflowers, peony poppies — hand-cleaned from varieties grown on the farm.

sellers.name: PepperHarrow Farm
sellers.description: 60-acre lavender and cut-flower farm selling a broad cut-flower seed list, including a celosia it introduced in 2025. Note: the list also includes standard commercial types whose per-packet origin is not stated.
sellers.orderingNotes: Seasonal: farm seed generally offered early January to end of February.

sellers.name: Stone Hollow Farmstead
sellers.description: Dahlia seed hand-harvested from open-pollinated Stone Hollow Farmstead dahlias on its own farm, sold by parent line.

sellers.name: Truelove Seeds
sellers.description: Farm-rooted seed company whose seed is grown by more than 70 small-scale urban and rural farmers (30% of each packet sale goes back to the grower); also grows wholesale cut flowers on its own farm.

sellers.name: Sweet Pea Gardens
sellers.description: Specialist sweet pea grower-shop carrying exhibition Spencer varieties in ~10-seed packets (found in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks).
sellers.orderingNotes: Specialty varieties are scarce and often out of stock; King's Ransom is limit 1 per household.

sellers.name: Sugar Moon Gardens
sellers.description: Small garden shop carrying exhibition sweet pea varieties (found in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks).

sellers.name: The Farmhouse Flower Farm
sellers.description: Flower farm shop carrying exhibition sweet pea varieties in ~10-seed packets (found in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks).

sellers.name: Neat Flower Farm
sellers.description: Flower farm shop found carrying Bix sweet pea in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks.

sellers.name: The Dahlia House
sellers.description: Shop found carrying Susan Burgess sweet pea in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks.

sellers.name: PNW Blooms
sellers.description: Shop found carrying Gerry Cullinan sweet pea in Hues' 2026-11-13 supplier checks.
